newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo says it has opened air corridor to Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Congo says it has opened air corridor to Burundi.

text.p: Congo said on Thursday that it had opened an air corridor to Burundi, which is under regional economic and transport sanctions.
Jean-Marie Kamba, a senior foreign ministry official, told a news conference that airlines LINA-Congo and Air-Burundi were each making two flights a week.
Under the arrangement, agreed in January, Burundi sends tea and coffee to Congo and Congo sends in fuel.
"The U.N. has not decreed the embargo and we, as a sovereign country, are therefore free to conclude what agreements we like," he said.
Kamba said that Burundi had asked Gabon, another oil producing nation, for a similar arrangement.
Regional states imposed economic and transport sanctions against land-locked Burundi last July after the Tutsi-dominated army seized power from a civilian Hutu president.
More than 150,000 people have died in massacres and civil war in Burundi between the army and Hutu rebels since the 1993 assassination of its first freely elected Hutu president.
